## Setup

To complete complete the tasks of this assignment, you will need to break your analysis into the following key steps:

1. find locations that experienced a blackout by creating a mask
2. exclude highways from analysis
3. identify homes that experienced blackouts by combining the locations of homes and blackouts
4. Below is guidance and suggestions for each of these steps.

Tip: For improved computational efficiency and easier interoperability with sf, I recommend using the stars package for raster handling.

Tip: Make sure to check that these datasets have the same coordinate reference systems! If not, transform them to match.

```{r}
library(terra) # raster handling
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap) # map making
library(here)
library(sf)
library(stars)
# library(spData) # spatial data
# library(spDataLarge) # spatial data
# library(geodata) # spatial data

# Set warnings to display as they occur
options(warn = 1)

# Set ggplot theme
set_theme(theme_bw())
```

```{r}
# Load night lights rasters - 2/7/2021
vnp_07_1 <- read_stars(here('texas_storm_crisis', 'data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif'))
vnp_07_2 <- read_stars(here('texas_storm_crisis', 'data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif'))

# Load night lights rasters - 2/16/2021
vnp_16_1 <- read_stars(here('texas_storm_crisis', 'data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif'))
vnp_16_2 <- read_stars(here('texas_storm_crisis', 'data', 'VNP46A1', 'VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif'))

# Load roads vector
# Use SQL query to only get rows where fclass = 'motorway'
roads <- sf::st_read(here('texas_storm_crisis', 'data', 'gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg'), query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")

# Load buildings vector
# Use SQL query to only get rows for residential buildings
builds <- sf::st_read(here('texas_storm_crisis', 'data', 'gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg'), query = "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")

```

## Data Merging

As mentioned above, Houston lies on the border of two tiles. You will need to combine these two tiles together to get one raster for each date (2021-02-07 and 2021-02-16). You can merge rasters using the method discussed in Lab 4, or, if you plan to use the stars package, you can combine them using st_mosaic.

```{r}
# Merge VNP 2/7 rasters
vnp_07_merged <- st_mosaic(vnp_07_1, vnp_07_2)

# Merge VNP 2/16 rasters
vnp_16_merged <- st_mosaic(vnp_16_1, vnp_16_2)
```

## Create blackout mask

To identify places that experienced a blackout, you should create a “mask” that indicates for each cell whether or not it experienced a blackout.

- find the change in night lights intensity (presumably) caused by the storm
    - hint: this will require creating a raster object for each day (2021-02-07 and 2021-02-16)

```{r}
# Warning - confirm VNP rasters match before proceeding
# Note: compare crs, resolution, and extent for operations
print("Checking that VNP rasters match in CRS, resolution, and extent...")
if (st_crs(vnp_07_merged)$epsg == st_crs(vnp_16_merged)$epsg){
    # CRS match - true
    print("VNP CRS do match!")
    if (all(st_res(vnp_07_merged) == st_res(vnp_16_merged))){
        # Resolution match - true
        print("VNP Resolutions do match!")
        if (all(st_bbox(vnp_07_merged) == st_bbox(vnp_16_merged))) {
            # Extent match - true
            print("VNP Extents do match!")
            print("Success - VNP rasters match in all required characteristics for operations.")
        } else {
            # Extent match - false
            stop("VNP Extents do NOT match!")
        }
    } else {
        # Resolution match - false
        stop("VNP Resolutions do NOT match!")
    }
} else {
    # CRS match - false
    stop("VNP CRS do NOT match!")
}
```

```{r}
# Create mask raster w/ the change (difference) in night light intensity
vnp_mask <- vnp_07_merged - vnp_16_merged
```

- reclassify the difference raster, assuming that any location that experienced a drop of more than 200 nW cm-2sr-1 experienced a blackout
- assign NA to all locations that experienced a drop of less than 200 nW cm-2sr-1 change

```{r}
# Reclassify using stars::cut()
vnp_rcl <- cut(vnp_mask,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 200, Inf),
  labels = c("OK", "BLACKOUT"))

# Assign NA to cells with a diff <= 200 nW cm-2sr-1
vnp_rcl[vnp_rcl == "OK"] <- NA
```

- vectorize the blackout mask
    - hint: use st_as_sf() to convert from a raster to a vector and fix any invalid geometries with st_make_valid()
```{r}
vnp_rcl_v <- vnp_rcl |> 
    # Convert raster to vector
    st_as_sf() |> 
    # Fix invalid geometries
    st_make_valid()
```

- crop (spatially subset) the blackout mask to the Houston area as defined by the following coordinates:
    - (-96.5, 29), (-96.5, 30.5), (-94.5, 30.5), (-94.5, 29)
- re-project the cropped blackout dataset to EPSG:3083 (NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area)

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Create bbox for houston based on above coords
houston_bbox <- st_bbox(
    c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
    crs = st_crs(vnp_rcl_v))

# Crop vnp_rcl vector data to houston bbox
houston_mask_v <- st_crop(vnp_rcl_v, houston_bbox) |> 
    # Reproject to projected 2D crs EPSG:3083 (NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area)
    st_transform(crs = "EPSG:3083")
```

## Exclude highways from the cropped blackout mask

Highways may have experienced changes in their night light intensities that are unrelated to the storm. Therefore, you should excluded any locations within 200 meters of all highways in the Houston area.

- identify areas within 200m of all highways
    - hint: you may need to use st_union

```{r}
# Warning - confirm roads and houston_mask_v match before proceeding
print("Checking that houston_mask and roads vectors match CRS...")
if (!(st_crs(houston_mask_v) == st_crs(roads))){
    # CRS match - false
    warning("CRS do NOT match! Reprojecting roads to match EPSG:3083...")
    roads <- st_transform(roads, crs = st_crs(houston_mask_v))
    print("CRS reprojection complete.")
}
print("CRS do match!")
```

```{r}
# Create 200m buffer around motorways in roads vector
motorway_buff <- roads |> 
    # Create the buffers
    st_buffer(dist = 200) |> 
    # Consolidate road and buffer geometries into one polygon to handle overlapping buffers
    st_union()
```

- find areas that experienced blackouts that are further than 200m from a highway

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Find geometries in houston_mask that do not intersect with motorway_buff
# st_difference - see Week 3 Lab
blackout_mask <- st_difference(houston_mask_v, motorway_buff)
```

## Identify the number of homes likely impacted by blackouts

- identify homes that overlap with areas that experienced blackouts

```{r}
# Warning - confirm builds and blackout_mask match before proceeding
print("Checking that blackout_mask and builds vectors match CRS...")
if (!(st_crs(blackout_mask) == st_crs(builds))){
    # CRS match - false
    warning("CRS do NOT match! Reprojecting builds to match EPSG:3083...")
    builds <- st_transform(builds, crs = st_crs(blackout_mask))
    print("CRS reprojection complete.")
}
print("CRS do match!")
```

```{r}
#| warning: false

# Find geometries in builds (residential polygons) that do intersect with blackout_mask
# st_filter, default = st_intersects - see Week 3 Lab
blackout_homes <- st_filter(builds, blackout_mask)

# Count number of residences (rows) impacted
num_blackout_homes <- nrow(blackout_homes)
```

## Data

Night Lights Data: NASA Level-1 and Atmosphere Archive and Distribution System (LAADS) DAAC. (2019). VIIRS/NPP Daily Gridded Day Night Band 500m Linear Lat Lon Grid Night (Collection 1) [Data set]. Goddard Space Flight Center. https://doi.org/10.5067/VIIRS/VNP46A1.001

Roads and Houses Data: OpenStreetMap contributors. (2021). Texas OpenStreetMap - roads and buildings [Data set]. Geofabrik. https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/texas.html
